prompt:
Architectural shell, fixed and unchangeable: Living room, rectangular, wider than deep, 4.5 m x 3.6 m; ceiling 2.8 m; continuous floor with no level changes. Left floor-to-ceiling window / balcony door wall 2.6 x 2.4 m, sill 0 m, 50% along the wall. Camera 1.5 m high, 4 m to the far wall, 24 mm lens, tilt -5 degrees, horizon 42% of frame height. The number of openings is exactly 1; do not add or remove any opening. Fixed features that stay: skirting board: low painted skirting along base of walls; wall-mounted air-conditioner: split-type indoor unit high on the long right wall near the left corner; electrical distribution box: recessed labelled panel high on the right wall; low wall access panel: small recessed labelled box low on the right wall; ceiling light fittings: two round flush-mounted ceiling fixtures.

Composition lock: single frame from the same camera position; two-point perspective, angled toward the front-left corner; horizon line at 42% of frame height; verticals truly vertical; -5 degree tilt; the room is not wider, deeper or taller than the dimensions above; mild 24 mm wide-angle perspective only, no fisheye, no added space at the frame edges.

Openings count lock: exactly 1 openings, on the described walls, at the described offsets and sizes; no added doors, no added windows, no added wall panels, no removed openings.

LIGHTING DESIGN
The room is lit by one key light: daylight entering from the left opening(s). Every shadow in the room runs away from that wall.
Practical fixtures are decorative only: at most two visible fixtures, warm 2700 K, low output. They do not cast shadows, do not add fill light, and do not glow.
No bloom, no halo, no light spill on the ceiling, no lens flare, no double shadows. The window stays readable, never blown to white.
Interior exposure is balanced for the room, not for the view outside.
Style-specific lighting: a paper globe pendant and a mushroom table lamp are the only practical fixtures, and the daylight reveals boucle nap, walnut grain and loose linen weave.
Keep window openings physically unchanged while changing what comes through them.

FURNISHING AND DECOR
Interior styling, in nordic: Airy Nordic rooms layer warm greige #A8A298, off-white #D5D8D1, light oak #C7B198, walnut #6D5B44, espresso ink #1A110C and cobalt #32445F accents with wabi-sabi warmth. Low wood platform beds, cane lounge chairs, oak sideboards, mismatched painted chairs, floating shelves; paper globe pendants, mushroom and arc lamps; striped cotton bedding, jute rugs, chunky knits, sheepskin; latex walls, herringbone wood, microcement, black iron.
Seating: low light-oak platform bed, off-white linen sofa, woven cane lounge chair, mismatched painted dining chairs; Table surfaces: round oak coffee table, slim oak writing table; Storage/display: wall-mounted oak bookshelf with visible books and ceramics, low oak sideboard with books and objects; Textiles: linen curtains, jute rug, striped cotton bedding, chunky knit throw, cobalt cushions, sheepskin on the cane chair; Appliances: matte black electric kettle, compact steel desk fan; Greenery: potted olive sapling, eucalyptus stems in a glass vase, trailing pothos; Wall decor: framed cobalt print, round walnut mirror, woven textile hanging; Tabletop objects: stacked art books, speckled stoneware mug, walnut tray with candle, cobalt glass carafe; Lighting fixtures: paper globe pendant, greige mushroom table lamp. Furnish the room with a low light-oak platform bed, off-white linen sofa, round oak coffee table, woven cane lounge chair, wall-mounted wood bookshelf, mismatched painted dining chairs, and a paper globe pendant above.
Density target: at least 12 distinct furnishing and decor items, at least 3 styled surfaces, 2 layered textiles per seating area.

Everything in the original room except the architectural shell is replaced: all furniture, soft furnishings, light fittings, textiles, decor and colours are new.

Hard corrections, these override other instructions: Restore the original straight wood-plank floor (remove herringbone), keep the wide full-wall left opening and the wider-than-deep room proportions with the source two-point front-left camera angle, and revert the ceiling to exactly two round flush fixtures with the AC near the left corner; remove the lit practical lamp so all shadows run only from the left window.

REALISM
Shot as an editorial interior photograph for a design magazine: 35 mm full-frame body, 24 mm tilt-shift kept level, natural imperfect surfaces - fabric wrinkles, curtain folds that are not perfectly symmetrical, faint scuffs on the skirting, real dust-free but lived-in tabletops, subtle sensor grain, gentle highlight rolloff. No retouching sheen, no HDR, no CGI, no archviz, no perfectly uniform material, no flawless symmetry, no plastic reflections.

Vertical 3:4 composition.
